source: Read the statement 'I take about 15 minutes to cycle from sc

items.question: Read the statement 'I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.' Why is it a statistical statement, and what data is behind it?
steps: The rider has cycled home on many days.
Each day took a slightly different time, for example 13, 16, 15 or 14 minutes.
The word about tells us the times vary.
The number 15 sums up all those days in one value.
A claim that sums up data in a number is a statistical statement.
items.answer: It is a statistical statement because 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day

videos.answer: It is a statistical statement because 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day

source: Which of these are statistical questions? (a) the price of a

items.question: Which of these are statistical questions? (a) the price of a tennis ball in India (b) the ages of the dogs on this street (c) the fraction of your class who like walking up a hill (d) Do you like reading? (e) about how many bricks are in this wall (f) the best bowler in yesterday's match (g) the rainfall pattern in Barmer last year
steps: (a) Prices differ between shops and brands, so we collect many prices: statistical.
(b) The dogs have different ages, so we collect each age: statistical.
(c) Each student answers yes or no, and the replies vary: statistical.
(d) This asks one person about themself, so there is one answer: not statistical.
(e) There is one wall and one count to estimate: not statistical.
(f) We compare the wickets and runs of several bowlers, which is data: statistical.
(g) The rainfall changes from day to day and month to month: statistical.
items.answer: (a), (b), (c), (f) and (g) are statistical questions; (d) and (e) are not

videos.answer: (a), (b), (c), (f) and (g) are statistical questions; (d) and (e) are not

items.question: Shubman scored 0, 17, 21 and 90 in four matches. Yashasvi scored 67, 55, 18 and 35. Compare them by highest score, total and the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
steps: Highest score: Shubman 90, Yashasvi 67.
Highest minus lowest: Shubman 90 − 0 = 90; Yashasvi 67 − 18 = 49.
Both played 4 matches, so the totals compare fairly: Yashasvi made 47 more runs.
Yashasvi's smaller difference, 49, shows he was more consistent.

source: In the second series Shubman scored 23, 7, 10, 52 and 18 in

items.question: In the second series Shubman scored 23, 7, 10, 52 and 18 in 5 matches. Yashasvi scored 26, 53, 2 and 15 and did not play one match. Who performed better on average?
steps: Shubman's total: 23 + 7 + 10 + 52 + 18 = 110 runs in 5 matches.
Yashasvi's total: 26 + 53 + 2 + 15 = 96 runs in 4 matches.
The totals come from different numbers of matches, so they do not compare fairly.
Shubman's mean: 110 ÷ 5 = 22 runs per match.
Yashasvi's mean: 96 ÷ 4 = 24 runs per match.
24 is more than 22, so Yashasvi performed better on average.
items.answer: Yashasvi, with a mean of 24 runs per match against Shubman's 22

videos.answer: Yashasvi, with a mean of 24 runs per match against Shubman's 22

source: Shreyas's group of 5 collected 3, 8, 10, 5 and 4 guavas. Par

items.question: Shreyas's group of 5 collected 3, 8, 10, 5 and 4 guavas. Parag's group of 6 collected 5, 4, 6, 3, 4 and 8 guavas. Each group shares equally. In which group does each member get more?
steps: Shreyas's group: 3 + 8 + 10 + 5 + 4 = 30 guavas.
Fair share: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 guavas each.
Parag's group: 5 + 4 + 6 + 3 + 4 + 8 = 30 guavas.
Fair share: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 guavas each.
Same total, but fewer people share it in Shreyas's group.
Each member of Shreyas's group gets 6 − 5 = 1 guava more.
items.answer: Shreyas's group: 6 guavas each against 5, so 1 more each

videos.answer: Shreyas's group: 6 guavas each against 5, so 1 more each

source: Vaishnavi counted 2, 7, 9, 4 and 3 hibiscus flowers blooming

items.question: Vaishnavi counted 2, 7, 9, 4 and 3 hibiscus flowers blooming on five days. Find the mean number of flowers per day and say what it means.
steps: Total flowers: 2 + 7 + 9 + 4 + 3 = 25.
Number of days: 5.
Mean: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 flowers per day.
If the same number bloomed every day, 5 would bloom each day.
Check by levelling: 9 gives 4 to 2 to make 5 and 6; 7 gives 2 to 3 and 4 gives 1 to 6, so all are at 5.
items.answer: 5 flowers per day on average

items.question: Identify a flowering plant in your neighbourhood. Track the number of flowers that bloom every day over a week during its flowering season. What is the average number of flowers that bloomed per day?
steps: This is a project: you observe a real plant for 7 days.
Sample data for a jasmine plant: 3, 5, 4, 6, 2, 5, 3 flowers.

Sample mean: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 flowers per day.

items.question: Two friends are training to run a 100 m race. Their running times over the past week are given in seconds: Nikhil: 17, 18, 17, 16, 19, 17, 18; Sunil: 20, 18, 18, 17, 16, 16, 17. Who on average ran quicker?
steps: Nikhil's total: 17 + 18 + 17 + 16 + 19 + 17 + 18 = 122 seconds in 7 runs.
Sunil's total: 20 + 18 + 18 + 17 + 16 + 16 + 17 = 122 seconds in 7 runs.
Both means: 122 ÷ 7 ≈ 17.43 seconds.
A smaller time means a quicker run, and the means are equal.
So on average neither ran quicker; Sunil's times vary more (16 to 20 against 16 to 19).
items.answer: They ran equally quickly on average: both means are 122 ÷ 7 ≈ 17.43 seconds

videos.answer: They ran equally quickly on average: both means are 122 ÷ 7 ≈ 17.43 seconds

steps: Sorted: 155, 160, 164, 165, 169, 173. Six values, so the median is (164 + 165) ÷ 2 = 164.5 cm.

steps: Total: 122, so the mean is 122 ÷ 15 ≈ 8.13 stories.

40 is far above the rest, so it is the outlier; the mean is above the median.
Without 40: total 82 in 14 values, mean 82 ÷ 14 ≈ 5.86 stories.
Median of 14 values: (5 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.5 stories.

items.question: A Grade 5 class has 17 boys and 11 girls with the heights in the table. Compare boys and girls, and count the students, and the boys, taller than the class mean.
steps: Boys: 128 to 158 cm, total 2430, mean 2430 ÷ 17 ≈ 142.94 cm, median 144 cm.
Girls: 136 to 156 cm, total 1616, mean 1616 ÷ 11 ≈ 146.91 cm, median 148 cm.
Whole class: total 4046, mean 4046 ÷ 28 = 144.5 cm, median 145 cm.
Girls have the higher mean and median, so girls are taller in this class on the whole.
But the tallest (158) and the shortest (128) are both boys, so not every girl is taller.
Heights above 144.5: 8 boys (145, 146, 146, 147, 150, 154, 155, 158) and 7 girls, 15 students in all.
items.answer: Girls are taller on the whole (mean ≈ 146.91 against 142.94); 15 students, of whom 8 are boys, are taller than the class mean of 144.5 cm

items.question: Rintu takes care of a date-palm tree farm in Habra. The heights of the trees (in feet) in his farm are given as: 50, 45, 43, 52, 61, 63, 46, 55, 60, 55, 59, 56, 56, 49, 54, 65, 66, 51, 44, 58, 60, 54, 52, 57, 61, 62, 60, 60, 67. steps: There are 29 trees, from 43 to 67 feet; the dots cluster from 50 to 62, with a stack of 4 at 60.

Trees shorter than 55.9 feet: 43, 44, 45, 46, 49, 50, 51, 52, 52, 54, 54, 55, 55, which is 13 trees.
Mean and median are close, so the heights are fairly balanced with no strong outlier.

items.question: The daily water usage from a tap was measured. The usage in litres for the first few days are: 5.6, 8, 3.09, 12.9, 6.5, 12.1, 11.3, 20.5, 7.4. (a) Can the mean or median daily usage lie between 25 and 30? Justify your claim using the meaning of mean and median. (b) Can the mean or median be lesser than the minimum value or greater than the maximum value in a data?
steps: The smallest value is 3.09 and the largest is 20.5.

(a) The mean is a fair share: levelling never lifts every value above the largest, so the mean is at most 20.5. The median is one of the middle values, so it is at most 20.5 too. Neither can lie between 25 and 30.
Check: total 87.39, mean 87.39 ÷ 9 ≈ 9.71 litres; sorted, the 5th value gives median 8 litres.
(b) No. Levelling moves amounts between values, so the level stays between the smallest and the largest; the median is a middle value of the sorted data.
items.answer: (a) No: mean ≈ 9.71 litres and median 8 litres, both between 3.09 and 20.5 (b) No, never

videos.answer: (a) No: mean ≈ 9.71 litres and median 8 litres, both between 3.09 and 20.5 (b) No, never

steps: Sumo total: 1201.9 kg, mean 1201.9 ÷ 5 ≈ 240.38 kg.

items.question: Draw the onion prices of the two towns as one double column graph with 1 unit = 10 rupees. In which months is the second town costlier, and by how much in September?
steps: Put the months in order along the horizontal line, two bars per month.
With 1 unit = 10 rupees, a price of 59 is 59 ÷ 10 = 5.9 units tall.
The second town's bar is taller in April (30 against 28), May (38 against 30), July (42 against 39), September (53 against 49) and October (60 against 56).
In June the two bars are equal at 35.
In the other 6 months the first town's bar is taller.
In September the difference is 53 − 49 = 4 rupees per kg.
items.answer: The second town is costlier in 5 months (April, May, July, September and October); in September by 4 rupees per kg

items.question: From the rocket graph (readings about SpaceX 31, 61, 96; Arianespace 15, 6, 3; ISRO 2, 5, 7; Galactic Energy 1, 2, 7), which organisations launched more rockets every year, and how did SpaceX change?
steps: Identify: 1 unit = 20 rockets, three bars per organisation in year order.
SpaceX: 31, 61, 96, so it rose every year; 61 is about twice 31, and 96 − 61 = 35 more in 2023.
Arianespace: 15, 6, 3, so it fell every year.
ISRO: 2, 5, 7 and Galactic Energy: 1, 2, 7 also rose every year.
Rocket Lab (6, 6, 9) and Expace (4, 4, 6) stayed the same once, so they did not rise every year.
items.answer: SpaceX, ISRO and Galactic Energy increased every year; SpaceX about doubled, then added about 35

videos.answer: SpaceX, ISRO and Galactic Energy increased every year; SpaceX about doubled, then added about 35

source: Using the readings CASC 48, 35, 45; Roscosmos 16, 21, 18; Ar

items.question: Using the readings CASC 48, 35, 45; Roscosmos 16, 21, 18; Arianespace 15, 6, 3; ISRO 2, 5, 7; Galactic Energy 1, 2, 7; SpaceX 31, 61, 96, decide which statements (a) to (f) are justified, and estimate the 2023 world total.
steps: (a) Not justified: Arianespace fell every year, and CASC fell from 48 to 35.
(b) Justified: only SpaceX (USA) passes 50, with 61 and 96; CASC's highest is about 48.
(c) Justified: France's Arianespace total is 15 + 6 + 3 = 24, less than 40.
(d) Justified: CASC total 48 + 35 + 45 = 128, average 128 ÷ 3 ≈ 42.67, around 40.
(e) Justified: ISRO 2 + 5 + 7 = 14 against Galactic Energy 1 + 2 + 7 = 10.
(f) Not justified: Roscosmos 16 + 21 + 18 = 55, less than 60.

items.question: City 1 had 564 hours of daylight in June and 186 in December; City 2 had 276 in June and 468 in December. Find the daylight per day in each case.
steps: June has 30 days: City 1 gets 564 ÷ 30 = 18.8 hours a day.
City 2 in June: 276 ÷ 30 = 9.2 hours a day.
December has 31 days: City 1 gets 186 ÷ 31 = 6 hours a day.
City 2 in December: 468 ÷ 31 ≈ 15.1 hours a day.
City 1 has its longest days in June; City 2 has its shortest days in June.
items.answer: June: City 1 18.8, City 2 9.2 hours a day; December: City 1 6, City 2 about 15.1 hours a day

source: Using daylight per day (City 1: about 6.8 in January, 18.8 i

items.question: Using daylight per day (City 1: about 6.8 in January, 18.8 in June, 6 in December; City 2: about 14.8 in January, 9.2 in June, 15.1 in December), describe both patterns and compare them with a full day.
steps: City 1 rises from January to a maximum in June, then falls to a minimum in December.
City 2 does the opposite: it falls to a minimum in June and rises to a maximum in December.
City 1's range is 18.8 − 6 = 12.8 hours; City 2's is 15.1 − 9.2 = 5.9 hours, so City 1 is more extreme.
A full day is 24 hours: 24 × 3 ÷ 4 = 18, so June daylight in City 1 is about three quarters of the day.
24 ÷ 4 = 6, so December daylight in City 1 is about a quarter of the day.
Opposite patterns point to opposite hemispheres: City 1 is Helsinki, City 2 is Wellington.
items.answer: City 1 peaks in June and City 2 in December; City 1 swings more (12.8 hours against 5.9), because the cities lie in opposite hemispheres, far from the Equator

items.question: The following infographic shows the speeds of a few animals in air, on land, and in water. Can we call this graph a bar graph? (a) What is the scale used in this graph? (b) What did you find interesting in this infographic? What do you want to explore further? (c) Identify a pair of creatures where one's speed is about twice that of the other. (d) Can we say that a sailfish is about 4 times faster than a humpback whale? Can we say that a sailfish is the fastest aquatic animal in the world?
steps: Yes: each animal's length along the speed line stands for its speed, as a bar does.
(a) The marks go up in equal steps of about 16 kilometres per hour (10 miles per hour each).
(b) Answers vary; for example, the peregrine falcon dives at about 322 kilometres per hour.
(c) Falcon 322 and swift about 170 (estimate, accept 160 to 180): 322 ÷ 170 ≈ 1.89, about twice. Sailfish about 109 and flying fish about 56: 109 ÷ 56 ≈ 1.95, about twice.
(d) Estimates from the bars: sailfish about 109 (accept 105 to 113) and humpback whale about 26 (accept 22 to 30): 109 ÷ 26 ≈ 4.19, so yes, about 4 times.
But only five water animals are shown, so the graph cannot say the sailfish is the fastest in the world.
items.answer: Yes, it is a bar graph with equal steps of about 16 kilometres per hour; falcon and swift are about twice; sailfish is about 4 times the humpback (estimates about 109, accept 105 to 113, and about 26, accept 22 to 30; 109 ÷ 26 ≈ 4.19), but fastest in the world cannot be told from five animals

items.question: The temperature variation over two days in different months in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, is given below. Draw a double-bar graph. Use the scale 1 unit = 4°C. Can you guess which two months these days might belong to? Times: 12 am, 3 am, 6 am, 9 am, 12 pm, 3 pm, 6 pm, 9 pm. Day 1: 20°C, 18°C, 16°C, 20°C, 26°C, 34°C, 30°C, 24°C. Day 2: 37°C, 34°C, 30°C, 33°C, 37°C, 43°C, 42°C, 39°C.
steps: With 1 unit = 4°C, 20°C is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 units and 43°C is 43 ÷ 4 = 10.75 units.
Draw two bars at each time, one for each day.
Day 1 runs from 16°C to 34°C, a range of 34 − 16 = 18°C, mean 188 ÷ 8 = 23.5°C.
Day 2 runs from 30°C to 43°C, a range of 43 − 30 = 13°C, mean 295 ÷ 8 = 36.875°C.
Cool nights near 16°C suggest winter, for example December or January.
Nights above 30°C and an afternoon of 43°C suggest peak summer, for example May or June.
items.answer: Day 1 is likely a winter day (December or January) and Day 2 a summer day (May or June)

items.question: The following clustered-bar graph shows the number of electric vehicles registered in some states every year from 2022 to 2024. (a) The data (rounded-off to thousands) for the states of Gujarat and Delhi are given in the table below (Gujarat 69000, 89000, 78000; Delhi 62000, 74000, 81000). Mark the corresponding bars on the bar graph. (b) Notice how the graph is organised, what scale is used, and what patterns the data shows. (c) How would you describe the change for various states between 2022 and 2024? (d) Approximately how many more registrations did Assam get in 2023 compared to 2022? (e) How many times more did the registrations in West Bengal increase from 2022 to 2024? (f) Is this statement correct: 'There were very few new registrations in Uttarakhand in 2023 and 2024, as the increase in the bar lengths is minimal'?
steps: (a) The guidelines are at 25000, 50000, 75000 and 100000. Gujarat's 89000 lies between 75000 and 100000; Delhi's 62000 lies between 50000 and 75000.
(b) Three bars per state for 2022, 2023 and 2024; 1 unit = 25000 vehicles; most bars grow left to right.

(c) Readings (estimates): Uttarakhand about 15000 to 19000, West Bengal about 10500 to 43000, Andhra Pradesh about 29500 to 55000, Odisha about 27500 to 62500, Assam about 40000 to 64500. Every state rose, Odisha by the most (62500 − 27500 = 35000); Gujarat rose then fell.
(d) Assam: about 60000 − 40000 = 20000 more.
(e) West Bengal: 43000 ÷ 10500 ≈ 4.1, about 4 times.
(f) Not correct: each bar counts that year's new registrations, about 16500 in 2023 and 19000 in 2024. Only the growth from year to year was small.
items.answer: (d) about 20000 more (e) about 4 times (43000 ÷ 10500 ≈ 4.1) (f) not correct: about 16500 and 19000 new registrations were made in those years; only the increase was small

items.question: Test the six statements against the table of average heights.
steps: 1. Justified: at every age both columns are higher in 2019 than in 1989, for example age 19 boys 163.5 to 166.5 and girls 151.9 to 155.2 (some ages dipped slightly in between, for example boys aged 15, 155.4 to 155.2 from 1989 to 1999).

source: Using the 2019 columns, find the largest growth between succ

items.question: Using the 2019 columns, find the largest growth between successive ages for boys and for girls. Then estimate heights for ages 1 to 4, and for age 12 in 2029.
steps: Boys aged 12 to 13: 148.4 − 142.2 = 6.2 cm, the largest jump for boys.
Girls aged 10 to 11: 138.6 − 132.8 = 5.8 cm, the largest jump for girls.
From 50 cm at birth to about 107 cm at age 5 is 107 − 50 = 57 cm, or 57 ÷ 5 = 11.4 cm a year if even.
Babies grow fastest in the first years, so estimates like 75, 87, 95 and 101 cm for ages 1 to 4 fit better than equal steps.
For 2029, add the 2009 to 2019 change again: boys aged 12, 142.2 + 3.3 = 145.5 cm; girls aged 12, 143.8 + 2.7 = 146.5 cm.
items.answer: Boys grew most from 12 to 13 (6.2 cm), girls from 10 to 11 (5.8 cm); ages 1 to 4 about 75, 87, 95 and 101 cm (estimates); age 12 in 2029 about 145.5 cm for boys and 146.5 cm for girls

items.question: Consider a group of 17 students with the following heights (in cm): 106, 110, 123, 125, 117, 120, 112, 115, 110, 120, 115, 102, 115, 115, 109, 115, 101. steps: The median is the 9th value, 115 cm: 8 students are on each side of it.

Mean: 1930 ÷ 17 ≈ 113.53 cm, close to 2019 averages for age 6 (113.1 and 112.9).
So the students are likely about 6 to 7 years old.

items.question: Find the 3-digit code from the five clues: 265 one right and in place; 271 one right but misplaced; 036 nothing right; 064 one right but misplaced; 542 two right but misplaced.
steps: 036 rules out 0, 3 and 6.
064 then has only 4 left, so 4 is in the code but not in the last place.
542 says 4 is not in the middle place either, so 4 is first.
265 has one digit in place; 2 cannot be first, so 5 is correct in the last place.
542 has two correct digits, 5 and 4, so 2 is out.
271 then needs 7 or 1 in a new place; only the middle is free, and 7 is already in the middle there, so 1 goes in the middle.
The code is 415; check: it fits all five clues.
